slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and in what package and at what price, to lift net revenue retention from 101% to 105% by 2028 while keeping gross margin at or above 75%?
Does Copilot create value that customers notice and that keeps them?
How many customers and prospects will pay, at what price and in what package?
Which package holds the 75% margin floor and closes the NRR gap?
Is the launch worth delaying the mobile app rewrite by two quarters?
How should we launch, and what tells us it is working?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO and executive team, approving the launch, package and engineering plan
Net revenue retention reaches 105% by 2028; Company gross margin stays at or above 75%; The two-quarter delay to the mobile app rewrite is worth what Copilot adds
January 2027 planning
Own AI model or a new provider; Core plan price; Mobile rewrite scope

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 in a per-seat Pro plan with a usage cap, not as a $149 add-on, and plan on $2.9M of ARR, not $8M
Copilot helps the volunteers who chose it, but its value for the base is unproven
–	Only 6% of accounts that left in 2026 left for AI features
Customers will pay, but plan on about $2.5–2.9M of first-year ARR, not the $8M forecast
–	14% bought at $149 when asked to pay; 46% said they would
–	The whole win-rate drop to Routewise is worth about $0.6M a year
Only a per-seat Pro plan with a usage cap holds margin above 75% and closes the NRR gap
–	A top-10% account would use 88% of a flat $149 price in inference
–	Pro hits 105% NRR if 26% of accounts move; 33% did in 2023
The launch is worth a two-quarter mobile delay, as long as the delay stops there
–	The delay risks at most $1.1M of ARR, 38% of what Pro adds
Launch Pro in Q2 2027, test it beyond volunteers, and return the team to mobile right after
–	Watch take-up against 26%, cost per seat and the mobile restart
